https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Async import of the appStore packages

golden_comments.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Performance — **Wrap app imports in thunks so the app store actually loads lazily**

Every `import("./x")` is a call that runs while the object literal is being built. All 29 app packages therefore start loading as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported. That is the same eager cost as the old static imports, so the stated goal of async loading is not met. It also makes things worse in two ways:

- Each package is now split into its own async chunk, which adds bundling overhead.
- If any app module fails to load (missing dependency, a throw at module evaluation), the rejected promise sits in the map. Until some code path happens to `await` that key, it is an unhandled rejection. In Node with default settings, that can crash the process even when the failing app is never used.

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **`getCalendarCredentials` now returns a Promise in `calendar`, which may break other callers**

`getCalendar` is now async, so the `calendar` field returned by `getCalendarCredentials` is a `Promise<Calendar | null>`. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. However, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (outside this diff) that checks `if (calendar)` or calls `calendar.method()` will now always see a truthy Promise and fail at runtime.

There is a second problem: these promises are created eagerly. If one rejects and is never awaited, it becomes an unhandled rejection.

I can't see all callers from this diff, so the severity is lowered.

golden_comments.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Download button inside the form likely submits the TOTP form again**

The Close and Copy buttons call `e.preventDefault()`, which suggests `Button` defaults to a submit button inside `<Form>`. The Download `Button` does not call it. Clicking Download would therefore likely run `handleEnable` again for a TOTP that was already enabled. That can show a spurious error or cause an unintended request.

Separately, putting a `<button>` inside an `<a>` is invalid interactive nesting and hurts accessibility.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~tsx
<Button
  color="primary"
  data-testid="backup-codes-download"
  href={backupCodesUrl}
  download="cal-backup-codes.txt"
  type="button">
  {t("download")}
</Button>
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **Copy shows the success toast even when the clipboard write fails**

`navigator.clipboard.writeText` returns a promise that can reject, for example on an insecure context or when permission is denied. The success toast is shown without waiting for it. A failure becomes an unhandled rejection, and the user believes the codes were copied.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
navigator.clipboard
  .writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))
  .then(() => showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success"))
  .catch(() => showToast(t("something_went_wrong"), "error"));
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Rename the BackupCode component, which is exported as `TwoFactor`**

The default export in `BackupCode.tsx` is named `TwoFactor`. This duplicates the name of the real TwoFactor component and is misleading in stack traces and React DevTools.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~tsx
export default function BackupCode({ center = true }) {
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Test — **Backup code login and disable flows have no tests**

None of the server-side behaviour that matters for security is tested:
- logging in with a backup code;
- rejecting a code that has already been used;
- disabling 2FA with a backup code.

The download content and clipboard content are also not checked.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~text
Add e2e tests: login with a backup code succeeds; reusing the same code fails with
incorrect_backup_code; disabling 2FA via "Lost access" with a backup code works.
~~~

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

golden_comments.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Restore the slug condition for organization creation**

The original code set `slug` only when billing is **disabled**: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The rewrite sets it only when billing is **enabled**, which flips the behavior.

The result:
- With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately, before payment or verification. It also duplicates `requestedSlug`.
- With billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug.

This change is also unrelated to the PR's purpose.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Restore the fallback to the destination calendar in Google update/delete**

The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that branch, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares each entry against that same falsy value, so it effectively always returns `undefined`.

Previously the code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now:
- `update` sends `calendarId: undefined`, which fails the API call.
- `delete` targets `primary` even when the event lives in another calendar.

This hits legacy references that have no `externalCalendarId`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without a credentialId**

`selectedCalendar` is now found only by matching `credentialId`. Destination calendars with a null `credentialId` are legacy records, handled by the `else` branch in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`. For those, no match is found, so the event is created in `primary` instead of the user's chosen calendar.

Before this change, `destinationCalendar.externalId` was used directly. Fall back to the first entry whose `credentialId` is unset.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const selectedCalendar =
  calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId ??
  calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => !cal.credentialId)?.externalId;
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Other calendar providers always use the main host's calendar for every host's credential**

`EventManager` now calls `createEvent` once per collective host, each time with that host's credential. However, Office365, CalDAV (base service) and Lark always pick `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the main host's calendar.

The effect for a non-main host's credential:
- **Office365:** it targets a calendar id that host doesn't own, which gives a 404 or the wrong calendar.
- **CalDAV:** the `filter` matches nothing, so no event is created.
- **Lark:** it uses the wrong calendar.

Use the `credentialId` now passed to `createEvent` to pick the matching destination, as the Google implementation does.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) {
  const destination =
    event.destinationCalendar?.find((c) => c.credentialId === credentialId) ??
    event.destinationCalendar?.[0];
  ...
}
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Team hosts' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar**

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing.

As a result, the collective hosts' destination calendars are ignored. This is the exact scenario the PR is meant to fix.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : [],
...
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];
}
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Video/conferencing references lose their credentialId**

Previously, non-calendar results stored `credentialId: result.credentialId`. Now non-calendar results (video apps such as Zoom or Daily) get `credentialId: undefined`.

Later update/delete paths that look up the video credential by `reference.credentialId` will no longer find it. Only calendar references should change.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined,
credentialId: result.credentialId,
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Dynamic users no longer select organization**

The refactor of `loadUsers` removed `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user query. Downstream code that reads `organizerUser.organization?.slug` (for example, booker URL generation) will silently get `undefined` for dynamic group bookings.

The change also alters error handling:
- An empty `dynamicUserList` now becomes a generic 500 instead of the previous behavior.
- Any `HttpError` (e.g. a 404) is rewritten to 400.

This depends on code outside the diff, which is why the severity is MEDIUM.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
select: {
  ...userSelect.select,
  credentials: true,
  metadata: true,
  organization: { select: { slug: true } },
},
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **updateEvent may be called with an undefined credential**

If the credential is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor in the DB (or has no app slug), `credential` stays `undefined`. It is still passed to `updateEvent`, which will throw or behave unpredictably.

Also, `credential` is declared outside the loop, so a value from a previous iteration could leak into the next one.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
let credential = this.calendarCredentials.find((c) => c.id === reference.credentialId);
...
if (credential) result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Restore logging of update failures**

`console.error(message)` was removed from the catch block, so failures while updating calendar events are now swallowed silently. Restore logging, preferably with the project logger.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
log.error(message);
~~~

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/2.pr_title: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries

golden_comments.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

review_comments.body:
**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Remove unreachable branches in getBaseConditions**

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a non-null `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. As a result, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch can never run, and neither can the final `NOTHING_CONDITION` branch.

The dead code is misleading. It suggests that filter conditions alone could act as the base condition when authorization is missing, which would be a security hazard if it were ever reachable.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const authConditions = await this.getAuthorizationConditions();
const filterConditions = await this.getFilterConditions();
return filterConditions
  ? Prisma.sql`((${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions}))`
  : Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`;
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Implementation — **Public `findMany` removed without visible migration of callers**

`findMany` was a public method and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions`, which has a different contract: it returns raw SQL instead of rows. Any existing callers, such as tRPC insights routers, would break at compile time. Callers that rely on `findManyArgs.where` merging would also lose behavior.

This diff does not show call-site updates. Verify that no callers remain outside these two files.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~text
grep for `insightsBookingService.findMany` / `.findMany(` on InsightsBookingService instances and migrate them to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions(), or keep a compatibility wrapper.
~~~

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7.pr_title: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

golden_comments.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Reliability — **Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget (unawaited promises)**

The old code collected the DB deletes and awaited them with `Promise.all`. The new code calls the async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` without awaiting them.

On serverless (Vercel/Next API routes) the function can be frozen once the response is sent. When that happens, the `cancelled` update, the row delete, or the Twilio/SendGrid cancel may never run, and the reminders are still sent.

The `try/catch` in `handleNewBooking` cannot catch any of these rejections, so it does nothing.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
await Promise.all(
  originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.map((reminder) =>
    reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL
      ? deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)
      : reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.SMS
      ? deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)
      : Promise.resolve()
  )
);
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Security — **Ownership scope dropped from reminder deletion**

The old code deleted reminders with `where: { id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } }`, which limited deletes to the caller's own bookings. The new helpers delete or update by `id` only.

This is only safe if `remindersToDeletePromise` already restricts results to the current user's bookings. That query is outside the diff, so I could not confirm it, hence the reduced severity.

Fix: confirm the upstream query filters by `booking.userId`. Alternatively, keep the ownership filter, for example by having the helpers use `deleteMany`/`updateMany` with that filter.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
// ensure upstream query includes:
where: { booking: { userId: ctx.user.id, eventTypeId: ... } }
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Type-only imports converted to value imports; possibly unused imports**

Several types are now imported as runtime values:
- `workflows.tsx`: `PrismaPromise` and `Prisma`. Their remaining uses were removed in this diff, so they may now be unused.
- `handleNewBooking.ts`: `App`, `Credential` and `EventTypeCustomInput`.

Under `isolatedModules` or `importsNotUsedAsValues`/`verbatimModuleSyntax` settings, these can cause lint or build errors. They also pull type-only symbols into the runtime import.

Fix: restore `import type` for the type-only symbols and remove any imports that are no longer used.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
import type { App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma } from "@prisma/client";
import { BookingStatus, SchedulingType, WebhookTriggerEvents, WorkflowMethods } from "@prisma/client";
~~~

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

golden_comments.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **"Unavailable all day" check compares Dayjs objects by reference**

`dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares two newly created objects, so it is always `false`. A full-day-off override (start equals end) is therefore never detected here. Such overrides are only partly caught by the later checks. A slot starting exactly at the override start is neither before the start nor after the end, so it is still offered.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
if (dayjs(date.start).isSame(dayjs(date.end))) return true;
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Slot end time ignored in the override and working-hours checks**

In the working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, not `slotEndTime`. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end is accepted.

The override check has the same problem. It tests `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)`, so a slot that starts inside the override but ends after it is accepted.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();
...
if (slotEndTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))) return true;
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Override day matched by UTC calendar date, not the organizer's local date**

The override start is converted to real UTC, and only its UTC date (`YYYY MM DD`) is compared with the slot's UTC date. For organizers far from UTC, one local day spans two UTC dates. Slots on the other UTC date are not recognised as belonging to the override day. They fall through to the working-hours check and may be offered or blocked incorrectly.

The working-hours check has a related risk: it uses `slotStartTime.day()` and hours in UTC. That is only correct if the `workingHours` passed in are expressed in UTC. That depends on code outside this diff.

A better approach is to compare the slot against the override's full UTC interval rather than its date string.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const overrideDayStart = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).startOf("day");
const sameDay = slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).isSame(overrideDayStart, "day");
~~~

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

golden_comments.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Sync endpoint returns a fetch `Response`, but callers expect SDK/axios shapes**

In sync mode, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `Response`. Several callers expect a different shape:
- Google reads `res?.data.access_token`.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `.data.error`.
- HubSpot treats the result as a token object.

On a `Response`, `.data` is `undefined`, so these paths throw `TypeError`, or silently store `undefined` tokens. The feature is broken for these apps as soon as `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set.

The helper also never checks `response.ok`, and it is typed `any`, which hides the mismatch.

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Zoho Bigin sends credentialId as the user id to the sync endpoint**

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential id where the user id is expected. The parent application will look up the wrong user, so it may return another user's tokens (cross-tenant leakage) or fail.

It also bypasses the `userId` null check meant to exclude team credentials.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
"zoho-bigin",
credential.userId // pass the user id, not credentialId
~~~

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **minimumTokenResponseSchema uses bogus computed keys and strips expiry/other fields**

`z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`, and so does the second computed key. The result is a single optional key literally named `"[object Object]"`, with the second definition overriding the first.

The effective schema is therefore `{ access_token: string }`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys:
- `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url` and similar fields are removed.
- Credentials saved from this result lose required fields. Salesforce, for example, loses `instance_url`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const minimumTokenResponseSchema = z
  .object({ access_token: z.string() })
  .passthrough();
~~~

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Placeholder `refresh_token` overwrites real refresh tokens**

When a provider omits `refresh_token` from a refresh response (which is valid in OAuth), the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"`.

Office365 then spreads this over `o365AuthCredentials`, replacing the user's real refresh token with a garbage value. Any app that merges parsed data the same way permanently loses the ability to refresh, and users must reconnect.

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Salesforce refreshes the token on every connection and uses fragile status check**

- Every `getClient` call now hits Salesforce's token endpoint and writes to the DB. There is no expiry check, and it bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the sync endpoint is never used for Salesforce. Yet it does use the minimal schema when sync is enabled, which strips `instance_url` (see issue 4).
- `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable: HTTP/2 responses have an empty `statusText`. Use `response.ok`.
- Lines 92-94 are dead code, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure.
- `HttpError` is not visibly imported in this diff. Verify it is imported.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const response = await refreshOAuthTokens(() => fetch(...), "salesforce", credential.userId);
if (!response.ok) throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Outbound sync request is unauthenticated**

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared secret or signature. The parent application cannot verify the request came from Cal.com. Anyone who can reach that endpoint could request live access tokens for arbitrary users.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
headers: {
  [process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]: process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET || "",
},
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Error handling changes leave dead branches and drop diagnostics**

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws on failure, so the existing `parsedToken.success` checks in Zoom and Office365 are dead code.

Office365 also lost the logging of the zod error and the Microsoft response. That makes token refresh failures much harder to debug. The thrown generic error discards the zod details as well.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

golden_comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Retry-count cleanup deletes reminders of every method, not just SMS**

The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter. This SMS cron job will therefore delete any `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount > 1`, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders.

Right now only this handler increments `retryCount`. Once the email or WhatsApp schedulers adopt the same field, which the generic column name invites, this job will silently delete their reminders. Those reminders may still be pending or managed by another cron.

Scope the condition to SMS.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
OR: [
  {
    method: WorkflowMethods.SMS,
    scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() },
  },
  {
    method: WorkflowMethods.SMS,
    retryCount: { gt: 1 },
  },
],
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Performance — **Unindexed `retryCount` predicate in an OR forces a table scan on every cron run**

Postgres cannot satisfy `(method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1` from the existing indexes. As a result, every cron invocation is likely to scan the whole `WorkflowReminder` table, which can be large.

Scope the condition to SMS (see issue 1) and add a supporting index. Another option is to split the cleanup into two separate `deleteMany` calls.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~prisma
@@index([method, retryCount])
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Normalize case before blacklist and duplicate checks**

The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the guest emails are not.
- A blacklisted address written with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) passes the check.
- The duplicate check against existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same person can be added twice under different casing.

The input array is also never de-duplicated on the server. The uniqueness refine exists only in the client schema.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const normalized = [...new Set(guests.map((g) => g.trim().toLowerCase()))];
const existing = new Set(booking.attendees.map((a) => a.email.toLowerCase()));
const uniqueGuests = normalized.filter((g) => !existing.has(g) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(g));
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Limit guest count and restrict who can trigger the emails**

The `guests` array has no maximum size. Any attendee, matched only by email, can add an unlimited number of arbitrary addresses. Each added address receives a booking email sent under the organizer's name. This can be abused for spam or bulk mailing through Cal.com's mail infrastructure. golden_comments.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the 4-argument version**

Ruby does not support overloading by arity. The new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at lines 149-151 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined at lines 145-147, so the earlier definition is dead code. Any existing caller that uses the old width/height form will now break:
- With 5 arguments (`downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)`), Ruby raises `ArgumentError` (given 5, expected 3..4).
- With 4 arguments (`downsize(from, to, w, h)`), `max_height` (an Integer) becomes `opts`. Then `opts[:allow_animation]` raises `TypeError`, or the dimension string is wrong.

I can only see the diff, so I can't confirm which callers use the old form (for example avatar or thumbnail generation). Grep for `OptimizedImage.downsize` / `downsize(` to check. Either way, the duplicate definition is a latent breakage.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def self.resize(from, to, width, height, opts={})
  optimize("resize", from, to, "#{width}x#{height}", opts)
end

def self.downsize(from, to, max_width_or_dimensions, max_height = nil, opts = {})
  if max_height.is_a?(Hash)
    opts = max_height
    max_height = nil
  end
  dimensions = max_height ? "#{max_width_or_dimensions}x#{max_height}" : max_width_or_dimensions
  optimize("downsize", from, to, dimensions, opts)
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Client-side size check hard-codes 10MB for all upload types, ignoring site settings**

The old code read `max_<type>_size_kb`, so it covered both images and attachments. The new code hard-codes 10MB for every type. This causes two problems:
- **Attachments larger than 10MB are blocked.** If an admin sets `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB, the client now rejects those files, even though nothing server-side was changed for attachments.
- **Attachments under 10MB pass the client check but fail later.** When `max_attachment_size_kb` is smaller than 10MB, the client accepts the file, it is uploaded, and only then is it rejected server-side. That wastes bandwidth and gives the user a worse error.

Only images get auto-downsized, so only images should use the relaxed limit.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~js
var maxSizeKB = type === 'image'
  ? 10 * 1024 // images are downsized server-side
  : Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'];
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Performance — **Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick runs per upload inside the request thread**

Each loop iteration shells out to ImageMagick on an image of up to 10MB, and this can happen up to 5 times while the web worker is blocked.

There is also no limit on pixel dimensions. A small, highly compressed file with huge dimensions (a decompression bomb) can use a lot of CPU and memory. Any user who can upload can trigger this repeatedly to tie up workers.

The return value of `downsize` is also ignored. If `convert` fails, the loop simply retries the same failing operation until it runs out of attempts.

Fix steps:
- Compute the target scale once from the size ratio instead of looping.
- Stop as soon as `downsize` returns false.
- Enforce maximum pixel dimensions or ImageMagick resource limits (`-limit memory`, `-limit area`).
- Consider doing the work in a background job.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
attempt = 5
while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes
  break unless OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)
  attempt -= 1
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **"80%" geometry may be invalid for the animated-GIF path**

When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled and the file is a GIF, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That method is outside this diff. If it uses gifsicle's `--resize-fit`, it expects a `WxH` geometry, and `"80%"` is not valid there. The command would fail every time, so large animated GIFs would never shrink and would then be rejected by the size validation.

Verify `downsize_instructions_animated`. If gifsicle is used, compute explicit pixel dimensions from the image's current size, or use `--scale 0.8`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
# compute explicit dimensions instead of a percentage
w, h = FastImage.size(tempfile.path)
OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "#{(w * 0.8).floor}x#{(h * 0.8).floor}", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Magic 10MB limit duplicated across client and server**

The 10MB ceiling is hard-coded in three places. It is not tied to any setting or to the web server's real body-size limit (for example nginx `client_max_body_size`).

These values can drift apart. When they do, users see a 413 error with a misleading "max 10MB" message, or the server and client disagree about which files are allowed.

Define the limit once, either as a site setting or a constant exposed to the client.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
# config/site_settings.yml (client: true)
max_image_upload_size_mb: 10
# controller
FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_upload_size_mb.megabytes, ...)
~~~

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Avoid breaking unsubscribe emails that don't pass `unsubscribe_url`**

The global `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` supplies that value. Other mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (for example digests) never pass it.

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Handle a missing TopicUser row in `unsubscribe`**

`TopicUser.find_by` returns `nil` when the user has no row for the topic. This happens when someone follows the link from a forwarded email, or when a different logged-in account opens it.

In that case `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError`, and the user gets a 500 error.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])
if tu.nil?
  TopicUser.change(current_user, params[:topic_id], notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted])
else

end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Stop changing state on a GET request (CSRF / link prefetch) and stop toggling on every visit** A plain GET changes the user's notification level. This causes three problems: - **CSRF:** any third-party page can embed `` and silently lower or mute a logged-in user's notification level for arbitrary topics. - **Prefetching:** email security scanners and link prefetchers will trigger the change before the user clicks. - **Not idempotent:** the logic lowers the level on every request. Watching → regular on the first visit, then regular → muted on a refresh or second visit. A page reload therefore changes state again. Fix: either require a signed per-user token in the link, or make the GET render a confirmation and perform the change via POST/PUT with CSRF protection. Also make the operation idempotent. **Proposed fix:** ~~~ruby # GET renders the page; actual change via: post "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe" # or validate params[:key] against a per-user/topic HMAC before mutating ~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Use `TopicUser.change` so the level change is published and the reason is updated**

Assigning `notification_level` directly and calling `save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`. That method publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus event and handles related bookkeeping such as `notifications_reason_id`.

As a result, open clients won't see the update, and the stored notification reason becomes stale.

~~~ruby
TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level)
~~~

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

golden_comments.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so the block can be bypassed**

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match on PostgreSQL. If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up as `Bad@Spammers.org` gets through. Nothing in this diff normalizes the email before storing or comparing it. The model's `uniqueness: true` and the unique index are also case-sensitive, so the same address can be stored twice with different casing.

Fix: downcase the email when saving it and when looking it up, or compare with `lower(email)`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
before_validation { self.email = email.try(:downcase) }

def self.should_block?(email)
  record = BlockedEmail.where(email: email.to_s.downcase).first
  ...
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Validation has a write side effect, and the counter update can lose increments**

`should_block?` runs inside a model validation, but it writes to the database. Every `valid?` / `save` attempt increments `match_count` and touches `last_match_at`. This includes repeated validation of the same record in one request and any availability-check endpoint that calls `valid?`. The statistics will therefore be inflated and do not reflect actual blocked signups.

The increment is also a read-modify-write (`match_count += 1; save`). Concurrent requests will lose updates.

Fix:
- Increment atomically in SQL.
- Consider separating the "check" from the "record a match" step.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def self.should_block?(email)
  record = BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first
  if record
    BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(["match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?", Time.zone.now])
  end
  record && record.action_type == actions[:block]
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and treats the setting as a raw regex**

This code was moved here unchanged, but it now lives in a new validator, so it is worth fixing. The regex `@(example\.com)` is not anchored at the end of the string, which causes two problems:
- **Whitelist bypass:** with `example.com` whitelisted, `x@example.com.attacker.org` passes.
- **Blacklist false positive:** with `spam.com` blacklisted, `x@spam.com.au` is rejected.

In addition, only `.` is escaped. Any other regex metacharacter in the setting is interpreted as regex syntax.

Fix: split the setting on `|`, escape each domain with `Regexp.escape`, and anchor the pattern with `\z`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def email_in_restriction_setting?(setting, value)
  domains = setting.split('|').map { |d| Regexp.escape(d.strip) }.join('|')
  value =~ Regexp.new("@(#{domains})\\z", true)
end
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **Any server-side email error permanently marks the email as "invalid" in the form**

The client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present. That includes errors that have nothing to do with blocking, such as "has already been taken" or a transient domain-setting error. From then on the field shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message instead of the real reason.

There are two further problems:
- `result.values.email` comes from the server's attributes. If the server normalizes the email (for example by downcasing it), it will not match what the user typed in `accountEmail`, so the client check never triggers.
- `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is declared on the class prototype, so the array is shared across controller instances.

Fix:
- Show the actual server error message rather than a generic "invalid".
- Initialize the array in `init`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~js
init: function() {
  this._super();
  this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]));
},
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Test — **Moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no tests in the new validator spec**

The spec only covers the blocked-email branch, and it does so with stubs. The domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator` but has no coverage here. The spec also does not check that the blocked check is skipped when a domain error was already added.

Fix: add cases that stub `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` and `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist`, and assert that `should_block?` is not called when a domain error already exists.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
it "adds an error when domain not in whitelist" do
  SiteSetting.stubs(:email_domains_whitelist).returns("example.com")
  BlockedEmail.expects(:should_block?).never
  validate
  record.errors[:email].should be_present
end
~~~

golden_comments.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

review_comments.body: **🟧 HIGH** · Security — **Imported HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization (stored XSS)** For `raw_html` posts, `cook` returns `raw` as-is. The RSS path HTML-unescapes `i.content` and passes it straight to `TopicEmbed.import`, with no sanitizer anywhere. The result lands in `post.cooked`, which is rendered with `raw` in the embed view and in the normal Discourse topic view. That means any `

**🟧 HIGH** · Security — **Unauthenticated callers can create unlimited topics by varying embed_url**

The only gate on the endpoint is the `Referer` header, and any non-browser client can forge it. The URL check in `TopicRetriever` only compares the host.

The throttle key is the full `embed_url`. Appending `?x=1`, `?x=2`, … yields distinct keys and distinct `TopicEmbed` rows. Each one:
- triggers a remote fetch,
- runs a full synchronous feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`),
- creates a brand-new topic as `embed_by_username`.

An anonymous attacker can therefore flood the forum with topics and make the server hammer the embedding site.

Fix:
- Normalize the URL (strip query string and fragment, or canonicalize it).
- Add a global or per-IP rate limit on retrievals.
- Optionally only create topics for URLs that appear in the feed, or for verified pages.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
# normalize before lookup/throttle
uri = URI(embed_url)
embed_url = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}#{uri.path}"
RateLimiter.new(nil, "embed-retrieve-#{request.remote_ip}", 10, 1.minute).performed!
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Kernel#open used on URLs (command execution risk, no timeouts)**

`open(url)` from open-uri falls back to `Kernel#open`. With that, a string starting with `|` executes a shell command.

`feed_polling_url` is an admin setting, and `import_remote` receives URLs from the disqus import and from the retriever. Today the retriever's host check incidentally blocks pipe strings, but that is fragile.

There are also no open/read timeouts, so a slow remote host can tie up Sidekiq workers. When called through `TopicRetriever`, the feed poll runs inside the retrieve job.

Fix: use `URI.parse(url).open(...)` or `Net::HTTP` with explicit timeouts, and only accept http(s) schemes.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
uri = URI.parse(url)
raise Discourse::InvalidParameters unless %w[http https].include?(uri.scheme)
body = uri.open(read_timeout: 10, open_timeout: 5).read
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Feed items without `content` crash the whole poll**

RSS 2.0 items usually provide `description`, not `content`/`content:encoded`. In that case `i.content` is nil, `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`, and the rest of the feed is aborted.

The same failure also breaks `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, which calls this job synchronously.

Fix: fall back to `description`, and skip items that have no content.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
raw = i.content || i.description
next if raw.blank?
content = CGI.unescapeHTML(raw.scrub)
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Stray `if` after `end` in ERB changes control flow**

`<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` followed by the next generated buffer-append statement. Ruby treats that statement as the modifier condition.

The template only works by accident, because the append happens to return a truthy value. It is confusing and could break with changes to ERB or the template.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~erb
<%- end %>
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Concurrent imports race on the unique embed_url index**

`import` does a check-then-create without a lock. Two concurrent workers can both see no embed; for example, the hourly poll and a retrieve job, or two retrieve jobs when staff bypass the throttle.

Both then create topics, and the second `TopicEmbed.create!` raises `RecordNotUnique`. The `Topic.transaction` may roll back the DB rows, but side effects queued by `PostCreator` (jobs, notifications) are not rolled back, and the job errors out.

Also, if `embed.post` is nil (the post was hard-deleted), `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will crash.

Fix: rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and return the existing post. Guard against a nil `embed.post`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
  TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first.try(:post)
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and mis-handles ports**

`//cdn.example.com/x.png` starts with `/`. The leading slashes are stripped, so it becomes `http://site.com/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which breaks external images and links.

The port check also omits the port only for 80 or 443, regardless of scheme. As a result, `https://host:80` produces `https://host` and `http://host:443` produces `http://host`.

Fix: use `URI.join(url, href)` for resolution.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
a['href'] = URI.join(url, href).to_s if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Disqus import loses category and created_at options**

The `--category` option was removed. The original `created_at` from the Disqus thread is no longer applied to the topic. Existing users of the thor task silently lose that behavior, and imported topics are dated "now".

Fix: pass `category` and `created_at` through `import_remote`/`import` to `PostCreator`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title], category: category_id, created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]))
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Editing existing migrations and using `force: true`**

This change modifies already-shipped migrations, which has no effect on databases that already ran them. It also adds `force: true`, which silently drops existing tables (and their data) if the migration runs against a DB where they already exist.

These changes are unrelated to the feature and risk data loss. Revert them.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
create_table :top_topics do |t|
~~~

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain

golden_comments.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Rename `include_website_name` to `include_website_name?` so the serializer calls it**

ActiveModel::Serializers only checks conditional inclusion methods named `include_<attr>?`, with a trailing `?`. `include_website_name` has no `?`, so the serializer never calls it. As a result:
- `website_name` is always serialized, as `null` when there is no website.
- The method is dead code that suggests a guard which does not exist.

No test covers the blank-website case, so this went unnoticed.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def include_website_name?
  website.present?
end
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **Fix the sibling-subdomain check, which treats unrelated domains as "same site"**

The equal-label-count branch drops the first label of each host and compares the rest. This is wrong for public suffixes:
- Instance `forum.co.uk` (or `example.co.uk`) and website `attacker.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`.
- Instance `meta.github.io` and website `someone.github.io` both reduce to `github.io`.

In these cases an unrelated third-party site is shown with its full path, as if it belonged to the instance. The impact is limited to display, but it weakens the purpose of the change, which is to show the full path only for same-site links.

Two further problems:
- The comparison is case-sensitive. `URI#host` keeps the user's casing, so `http://Example.com/user` will not match `example.com`.
- The URL is parsed up to three times (`URI(website.to_s)` is repeated).

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def website_name
  uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil
  return if uri.nil? || uri.host.nil?
  website_host = uri.host.downcase
  discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname.downcase
  same_site =
    website_host == discourse_host ||
    discourse_host.end_with?(".#{website_host}") ||
    (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length &&
     discourse_host.split('.').length > 2 &&
     website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]) # consider PublicSuffix here
  same_site ? website_host + uri.path : website_host
end
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **Website values without a scheme are hidden from the profile**

`URI("example.com/user").host` is `nil`, so `website_name` returns `nil` for any website stored without `http://` or `https://`. The template now gates the whole globe/link block on `model.website_name`, so such websites are not shown at all.

This is only a problem if stored website values can lack a scheme. Normalization (for example, prepending `http://` on update) happens outside this diff, so this is unverified. If legacy or unnormalized data exists, fall back to a scheme-prefixed parse or to the raw value.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
raw = website.to_s
raw = "http://#{raw}" unless raw =~ /\A[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//i
uri = URI(raw) rescue nil
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Avoid mutating a string literal with `<<`**

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal. It works today, but it raises `FrozenError` if `# frozen_string_literal: true` is enabled, which is a common migration step. Use interpolation instead.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
discourse_host.end_with?(".#{website_host}") ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Test — **Add specs for the untested branches and edge cases**

The new specs cover exact match, unrelated domain, and parent domain. They do not cover:
- the sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`);
- a blank website (which would have exposed issue 1);
- unparsable or scheme-less URLs;
- the public-suffix false positive (`a.co.uk` vs `b.co.uk`).

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
it "returns complete path for sibling subdomain" do
  user.user_profile.website = 'http://www.example.com/user'
  Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('forum.example.com')
  expect(json[:website_name]).to eq 'www.example.com/user'
end

it "omits website_name when website is blank" do
  user.user_profile.website = ''
  expect(json).not_to have_key(:website_name)
end
~~~

The original light-theme value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code changes the light branch to 70% and the dark branch to 30%, which swaps the two values.

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: FIX: proper handling of group memberships

golden_comments.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Validate and bound `limit`/`offset` on the public members endpoint**

`limit` and `offset` come straight from the request with only `to_i` applied. This causes two problems on this public, non-admin endpoint:
- **Unbounded size:** any visitor can request `limit=10000000` and force a huge query plus serialization, which is a cheap DoS vector.
- **Server errors:** negative values (`limit=-1` or `offset=-5`) make PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative", which returns a 500.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
limit  = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 200].min
offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 users**

Previously, non-automatic groups returned all their members. The endpoint now always paginates with a default of 50.

The public `group/members` template iterates `members` but has no pagination controls. Any group with more than 50 members therefore only ever shows the first 50, with no way to see the rest.

Fix: add next/previous controls (or infinite loading) to the public members page, reusing `offset`/`limit` on the model.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~
Add pagination actions to the group-members controller (mirroring admin-group next/previous) and render controls in group/members.hbs.
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Adding an already-present member may raise and return a 500**

`group.add(user)` is called for every username, with no check for existing membership. If `group.add` appends to `users` and `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, re-adding an existing member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. That aborts the whole request with a 500 and can leave the batch partially applied.

This depends on the `Group#add` implementation and the indexes, which are not shown in the diff.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
existing = group.user_ids.to_set
usernames.split(",").each do |username|
  user = User.find_by_username(username.strip)
  group.add(user) if user && !existing.include?(user.id)
end
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Test — **Specs rely on a hard-coded group id and use the wrong HTTP verb**

- **Hard-coded id:** several tests assume `Group.find(1)` exists and is automatic (the seeded "everyone" group). That is brittle and depends on seed data and sequence state.
- **Wrong verb:** the `remove_member` automatic-group test uses `xhr :put` even though the route is `DELETE`.

Fabricate an automatic group explicitly and use the correct verb.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
it "cannot remove members from automatic groups" do
  group = Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)
  xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: 42
  response.status.should == 422
end
~~~

golden_comments.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Fallback locales are loaded only in the web request path, not in jobs, mailers or console**

`translate` still loads only `config.locale` (line 68). The fallback locales (the site default and `:en`) are loaded only when `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` runs, and that call exists only in the controller's locale setup.

Code that sets `I18n.locale` outside a controller never makes that call. This includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks and the console. In those paths the `Fallbacks` backend walks `[user, site, :en]`, but the extra locales were never loaded. The result is "translation missing" instead of the intended fallback.

This is fragile because every new entry point must remember to call `ensure_loaded!`.

The fix is to load the whole fallback chain inside `translate`, or inside `load_locale`, instead of relying on callers.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def translate(key, *args)
  I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].each do |l|
    load_locale(l) unless @loaded_locales.include?(l)
  end
  ...
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **The translation cache key ignores the site default locale, so fallback results leak or go stale**

`FallbackLocaleList#[]` now makes the result of a lookup depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. That value is per-site in multisite, and admins can change it at runtime.

The translate_accelerator cache is outside this diff. As far as I know, it is keyed only on key, `config.locale` and backend. If so, two problems follow:
- A fallback string computed for site A (default `fr`) can be served to site B (default `de`) when both have a user with the same missing locale.
- After an admin changes the default locale, the old fallback strings stay cached.

Severity is reduced because this depends on cache-key code not shown in the diff. The fix is to include the full fallback chain, or at least `SiteSetting.default_locale`, in the cache key. Alternatively, clear the cache when the default locale changes.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
k = "#{key}#{I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].join(',')}#{config.backend.object_id}"
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **Make the fallback list robust to a nil default locale and to string locales**

There are two problems on this line:
- **Nil default locale:** `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises `NoMethodError` if the setting is nil. This can happen early in boot, during asset precompile without a DB, or during tests. The `.compact` call comes too late to help.
- **String locales:** `locale` can be passed as a String, for example via `I18n.t(..., locale: "en")`. In that case `.uniq` does not dedupe `"en"` against `:en`. The duplicate locale then gets checked twice, and `@loaded_locales.include?` checks may be inconsistent.

The fix is to normalize to symbols and compact before calling `uniq`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def [](locale)
  [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en].compact.map(&:to_sym).uniq
end
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **The Hash subclass only partly implements the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks interface**

`FallbackLocaleList` subclasses `Hash` and overrides only `[]`. Some libraries, and newer i18n versions, may call other `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` methods such as `defaults`, `defaults=` or `map`. Rails' own i18n railtie does this when `config.i18n.fallbacks` is configured. Those calls would fail or silently do nothing.

It is safer to subclass `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` and override `[]` and `compute`. That keeps API compatibility.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
class FallbackLocaleList < I18n::Locale::Fallbacks
  def [](locale)
    [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en].compact.map(&:to_sym).uniq
  end
  ...
end
~~~

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding

golden_comments.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Migration crashes when `embed_category` is not set**

`execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns a row. On a fresh install, or on any site that never set `embed_category`, the JOIN returns zero rows. `PG::Result#[]` then raises, or returns nil and `nil['id']` raises. The migration aborts and the deploy is blocked.

The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same flaw. That setting is not always present as a row in `site_settings`, because defaults are not stored.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
rows = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")
category_id = rows.cmd_tuples > 0 ? rows[0]['id'].to_i : 0

if category_id == 0
  rows = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")
  category_id = rows.cmd_tuples > 0 ? rows[0]['value'].to_i : 0
end
~~~

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Migrated hosts are unescaped and not normalized, so existing embeds break**

There are two problems with how existing hosts are copied over:

- **Unescaped SQL.** Each host string is interpolated directly into the SQL. A value containing `'` breaks the migration, and the pattern is SQL injection–prone.
- **No normalization.** The old setting explicitly allowed values such as `http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`, and entries with trailing whitespace or `\r`. These are inserted verbatim. The raw SQL bypasses the model's `before_validation` stripping.

`record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` (for example `example.com`), so any legacy entry that has a scheme, path, or trailing whitespace never matches. Existing embeds silently stop working after upgrade.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
records.map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).each do |h|
  h = h.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at)
           VALUES (#{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)}, #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Host lookup is case-sensitive on the input side and never matches hosts stored with a port**

- **Case.** `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the DB column but not the incoming value. `URI("http://EvilTrout.com").host` keeps its case, so referers with uppercase letters are rejected.
- **Port.** The validation regex allows `example.com:8080`, but `uri.host` drops the port. A host stored with a port can therefore never match.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
host = uri.host
return false unless host.present?
host = "#{host}:#{uri.port}" if uri.port.present? && ![80, 443].include?(uri.port)
where("lower(host) = ? OR lower(host) = ?", host.downcase, uri.host.downcase).first
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **`before_validation` raises on nil host**

`self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil. This happens with `EmbeddableHost.new`, or when the param is missing in `save_host`. The result is a 500 instead of a validation error.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
before_validation do
  if host.present?
    self.host = host.strip.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')
  end
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Admin host endpoints 500 on unknown id or missing params**

- **Unknown id.** `where(id:).first` returns nil for an unknown id. `nil.destroy`, or `nil.host=` inside `save_host`, then raises `NoMethodError`.
- **Missing params.** `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises when the root key is missing.
- **Unvalidated category.** `category_id` is not validated to reference an existing category. There is no FK and no model validation, so a bogus id is accepted and later used when creating topics.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
def update
  save_host(EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]))
end

def destroy
  EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]).destroy
  render json: success_json
end

def save_host(host)
  attrs = params.require(:embeddable_host)
  host.host = attrs[:host]
  # ...
end
# model: validates :category, presence: true
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Maintainability — **Fabricator file contents are swapped**

`category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `:embeddable_host`. The new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works only because all fabricator files are loaded, but it is clearly a mistake and will confuse future maintainers.

**🟦 LOW** · Bug — **`replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore**

`String#replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. A type such as `site_customization_foo` would not be normalized. Use a global regex instead.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~js
if (ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace(/_/g, '-')) !== -1) { return "/admin/"; }
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Test — **Spec is misleading and the store test assumes behavior the mock doesn't provide**

golden_comments.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Denial cache hides newly granted permissions for the whole TTL**

The new `Check` flow is built to pick up fresh grants. When the cached permission map does not allow access, it falls back to the database (see the "outdated cache" test).

The denial cache undoes this. Once a deny for `(user, action, name, folder)` is cached, `Check` returns `Allowed: false` at line 117. It never consults the permission cache or the DB for `shortCacheTTL`.

So a user who has just been granted access, or whose dashboard was just moved into an accessible folder, keeps being denied. Nothing invalidates this cache. Users will see "I was given access but still get 403" bugs.

The client-side cache was also removed for in-proc calls, specifically to reduce staleness. That makes this regression more visible.

Fix options:
- Use a much shorter TTL for denials.
- Invalidate denial entries when role, team or permission changes are written.
- Or drop the denial cache and rely on singleflight plus the permission cache.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~go
// in NewService
permDenialCache: newCacheWrap[bool](cache, logger, denialCacheTTL), // e.g. a few seconds
// and/or delete matching denial entries on permission writes
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Performance — **Denial cache keyed per resource name can grow without bound**

Every denied `Check` stores one entry per `(namespace, user, action, name, parent folder)`. The values come straight from the request.

A caller that iterates many names or folders, or a large dashboard listing done via per-item checks, creates one local-cache entry per resource. These live in the shared cache that also holds permissions, teams and folder trees.

Before this change, cache size scaled with users × actions. It now scales with users × resources. This raises memory use and cache churn, and gives a cheap way to inflate memory with arbitrary names.

Fix options:
- Bound the cache.
- Use a short TTL.
- Or cache denials at a coarser granularity.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~go
// Prefer a bounded/LRU cache for denials, or skip caching when Name is empty/unknown,
// and keep the TTL short.
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Performance — **Cached-deny path does duplicate work and records a cache hit as a miss**

When cached permissions exist but do not allow access, `Check`:
- resolves user identifiers again inside `getIdentityPermissions`,
- re-runs the DB permission fetch, and
- evaluates `checkPermission` a second time.

That is roughly double the work on every first-time deny.

It also increments `permissionCacheUsage{"false"}` even though the cache was hit. This skews the hit/miss metric that this PR reorganizes.

Errors from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (for example a DB error from `GetUserIdentifiers`) are silently treated as a miss. Consider distinguishing `cache.ErrNotFound` from real errors.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~go
cachedPerms, err := s.getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)
switch {
case err == nil:
	s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("true", checkReq.Action).Inc()
	// ... check, return if allowed
case !errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound):
	ctxLogger.Warn("cache lookup failed", "error", err)
	s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()
default:
	s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()
}
~~~

**🟦 LOW** · Maintainability — **Cache lookup removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions affects all callers**

`getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` no longer read `permCache`. They only write it. Any caller of `getIdentityPermissions` other than `Check` and `List` now always hits the database. Such callers cannot be seen in this diff and would need checking.

The test case covering the cache-hit behavior was deleted rather than moved. The read/write split between `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and these functions is also easy to misuse.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~go
// Either document that getIdentityPermissions is "force refresh" only,

~~~
